paragraphs: Mispar harema"ch tebot diqriat shema hu kak shishsha d"shema yisrael" veshishsha d"baruk shem kebod malkuto leolam vaed", vm"b d"veahabta", v"b shel "vehaya im shamoa" ad "vesamtem", venu"n d"vesamtem" ad "vayyomer", vs"t d"vayyomer" hare sak hakkol rm"h veim g' tebot shekkopel hashlicha tzibbur nishlamim rm"ch tebot, veyadua ki bemispar harema"ch hannizkar yesh kavvanot amuqqot bekol happeratim vei epshar lihyot nechsar etzel kol echad veechad mimmispar harema"ch kelum, velaken gam hayyachid haqqore qeriat shema ben deshacharit ben dearbit ben qeriat shema sheal hahamata tzarik likpol shelosh tebot "Adonai elohekem emet" kede lehashlim harema"ch, mihu hashshalicha tzibbur mitztzad bechinato yesh lo koach yoter behashlama zo shel kepel shelosh tebot hannizkarot velaken im haadam mitpallel im tzibbur sheyyesh sham shelicha tzibbur omed yishma hakkepel min hashlicha tzibbur vehu eno tzarik likpol ella raq yekavven lehashlim rm"ch shello min shemiato hakkepel mehashlicha tzibbur ubesipri haq' "mqbtzyl" haaleti besiyyata dishmayya deim hammitpallel im hahitzbur odennu beemtza qeriat shema vehashshalicha tzibbur hishlim haqriat shema vekapal shelosh tebot hannizkarot la mehanne lehashlim leatzmo mikkoach shemia mehashshalicha tzibbur, ki sodan shel debarim tzarik lihyot mispar zeh shel hakkepel baacharona bigmar haqriat shema veim yashlimu baemtza hare zeh meareb hasseder lihyot tachtonim lemala, lekak bikhay gavna adip tepe shehu atzmo yikpol veyashlim hachissaron veraq im hu gomer haqriat shema im hashlicha tzibbur adip tepe lishmoa hakkepel mishshelicha tzibbur:

clarification.explanation: The count of the 248 words of the Shema: 6 of "Shema Yisrael," 6 of "Baruch Shem Kevod Malchuto," 42 of "Ve'ahavta," 72 of "Vehaya Im Shamoa" until "Vesamtem," 50 from "Vesamtem" until "Vayomer," and 69 of "Vayomer" — that comes to 245, and with the three words that the prayer leader repeats they are completed to 248. In this count there are profound intentions in every detail, and it is impossible for a person to be missing any of it. Therefore even an individual reciting the Shema (Shacharit, Arvit, or on the bed) must repeat the three words "Hashem Elokeichem Emet" to complete the 248. But the prayer leader, by virtue of his role, has greater power in this completion; therefore one who prays with a congregation that has a prayer leader should hear the repetition from him and intend thereby to complete his own 248, and need not repeat it himself. Nevertheless (Makbetziel): if he is still in the middle of the Shema and the prayer leader has already finished and repeated the words — it will not help him to complete it by that hearing, since the secret of the matter is that the repetition must come last, at the end of the reading, and completing it in the middle would mix up the order; therefore in this case it is better that he repeat it himself. Only if he finishes the Shema together with the prayer leader is it better to hear the repetition from him.
takeaways: The Shema has 248 words — 245 in the reading itself plus 3 that the prayer leader repeats ("Hashem Elokeichem Emet"); an individual must repeat them himself to complete the count.

One praying with a congregation should hear the repetition from the prayer leader and intend to complete his count that way — but only if he finishes together with him, not if he is still in the middle.

paragraphs: Ap al pi demin hattora chiyyub qeriat shema hu shettayim achat beshacharit veachat bearbit, tiqqenu chaza"l arbaa peamim qeriat shema vekullam hem letzorek hayyichud vehazzivvug hannaaseh lemala bibchinat v"h shebbashshem, veellu haarbaa qeriat shema enam shavim bemaalatam, vezeh sidran bemaalatam mimmatta lemala vehu dehaggerua mikkullam hi qeriat shema sheal hammitta, ulemala mimmenna qeriat shema dearbit, ulemala mizzo qeriat shema deqarebbanot, ulemala mizzo qeriat shema di"yotzer" vezo hi hamulla shebbekullam, veal yachshob haadam diqriat shema deal hammitta baabur shemira min hammazziqin hu, ella zo hi taqqanat chaza"l kede lehamshik bah orot letzorek hayyichud vehazzivvug hannaaseh lemala bachatzot hashsheni shel hallayla shehu matmid venimshak ad or habboqer, dehamshakat orot ellu al yede qeriat shema zo yitqayyemu ad or habboqer, veachar het hayyom barur yistallequ vetzarik lehachazir otam mechadash achar habboqer, umeachar dachatzi harishon shel hayyom hu meulleh meod, lekak hayyichud vehazzivvug hannaaseh bo bitpillat shacharit hu gam ken gadol umeulleh meod, ulepi godel erko tzarik lo hakana gedola biqriat shema, veap al gab diqriat shema d"yotzer" hi gedola meod vehayyichud hannaaseh bah hu nelam umeulleh meod im kol zeh lo yaspiq haadam lehashlim hattiqqun harauy lizman tepillat shacharit biqriat shema d"yotzer" bilbad, mippene ki en lanu yekolet lehamshik kol haorot hatztzerikim lizman zeh mikkol hammadregot bepaam achat kelomar biqria achat d"shema", ulekak tiqqenu chaza"l qodem qeriat shema zo d"yotzer" ad qeriat shema deqarebbanot sheanachnu omerim otah qodem parashat hattamid, kede shennimmeshik haorot bahadragot ditchilla nimmeshik al yede qeriat shema deqarebbanot or bechina achat, veachar kak al yede qeriat shema d"yotzer" nimmeshik od or bechina achat shehu maqom yoter gabohha alayv, veaz al yede zeh achar kak naasa hayyichud vehazzivvug bitpillat shacharit: vehinneh chasidim harishonim shenniqrain vatiqin shehayu nizharim liqrot qeriat shema d"yotzer" qodem hanetz hachamma vegomerin otah im hanetz hachamma lo hayu tzerikin liqrot qeriat shema deqarebbanot mippene ki al yede godel veotzem chasidutam haya lahem koach gadol bekavvanatam umachshabtam, vegam od shehem maqdimim liqrotah qodem hanetz hachamma shehu samuk mammash lehistallequt otam haorot shel chatzot layla, al ken en tzarik sheyyamshiku haorot haelyonim letzorek tepillat shacharit behadragot kaasher anachnu tzerikin, ella day lahem limshok orot hatztzerikin litpillat shacharit biqriatam bepaam achat, abal baddorot haacharonim en kol adam rauy lekak velaken atta apillu chasidim hammitpallelin tepillat havvatiqin sheqqorin qeriat shema qodem hanetz hachamma, tzarik sheyyiqreu qeriat shema shette peamim achat deqarebbanot veachat deyotzer: veotah haqriat shema dearbit hi letzorek hamshakat orot hatztzerikin leyichud vezivvug hannaaseh bitpillat arbit, abal letzorek hayyichud vehazzivvug hannaaseh bitpillat hammincha en anachnu tzerikin liqro qeriat shema, ki yaspiqu lah otam haorot shennimsheku biqriat shema deshacharit deap al gab denistallequ achar hattepilla im kol zeh lihyot ki hayyom hu "chesed" veen haddinim sholetim kol kak en mistalleqim legamre umishtayyer mehem, vezeh hashshiyyurin yaspiqu litpillat hammincha bilbad, velaken meulleh hayyichud vehazzivvug hannaaseh bitpillat shacharit al hannaaseh bitpillat hammincha meod meod, yaan ki mah shennaasa bemincha hi min hashshiroyn deorot hammochin shel shacharit, ulekak haddinin mitgabberin bitpillat hammincha lepi sheorot hammochin holekim umitmaatin, vehattaam dela taspiq qeriat shema dearbit letzorek gam mah shennaasa bachatzot shelitat dinin gemurim, ulekak achar tepillat arbit yistallequ orot shennimsheku al yede qeriat shema legamre, velaken tzerikin anachnu liqro qeriat shema al hammitta bishbil tzorek chatzot hashsheni shel hallayla, umah shemmeqaddemin liqro qeriat shema zo beet hashshekiba veen mamtinim ad sheyyaggia chatzot hashsheni shel hallayla yitbaer inyan zeh leqamman bimqomo, vekol zeh shekkatabnu hu rashe debarim mah sheyyukal adam pashut lisbol bedato, ak beemet debarim ellu yesh bahem od sodot amuqqim venitbaaru berachebbah beshaar hakkavvanot lerabbenu haari"y za"l:

clarification.explanation:
Although from the Torah the obligation to recite the Shema is twice a day (Shacharit and Arvit), the Sages instituted four recitations of the Shema, and all of them serve the union and pairing accomplished above (in the aspect of the letters Vav-Heh of the Name). These four recitations are not equal in level; their order from lowest to highest is: the Shema on the bed, the Shema of Arvit, the Shema of the sacrifices, and the Shema of "Yotzer" — the highest of all.

Let a person not think that the Shema on the bed exists only for protection from harmful forces; the Sages instituted it in order to draw lights for the sake of the union accomplished at the second midnight of the night, which continues and stands until the light of morning. Since the first half of the day is very exalted, the union accomplished in it in the Shacharit prayer is also very great and exalted, and it requires great preparation in the Shema. Although the Shema of "Yotzer" itself is great and exalted, we are not able to draw down all at once (in a single recitation) all the lights needed for this time from every level — therefore the Sages also instituted the Shema of the sacrifices (recited before the portion of the Tamid), which first draws down light of one aspect, and after it the Shema of "Yotzer" draws down a higher light — and only thus is the union needed for the Shacharit prayer completed. The ancient Vatikin, who recited the Shema of "Yotzer" right up against sunrise (very close to the departure of the lights of midnight), did not need the Shema of the sacrifices, because by the power of their holiness and intention they drew all the lights in a single recitation; but in the later generations we do not have such power, and therefore even those who pray as the Vatikin must recite the Shema twice — of the sacrifices and of "Yotzer."

The Shema of Arvit is intended for drawing the lights needed for the union accomplished in the Arvit prayer. By contrast, for the Minchah prayer there is no need for a separate Shema, because the remainder of the lights already drawn in the Shema of Shacharit suffices — since during the day (which is the quality of "chesed," and judgment does not dominate) the lights do not depart entirely after the prayer, and a remainder of them stays until Minchah. For this reason the union accomplished in Shacharit is far more exalted than that of Minchah, since in Minchah it is accomplished only from the remainder of the lights of Shacharit, and their power keeps diminishing. However, the Shema of Arvit itself is not sufficient for the sake of the union accomplished at midnight (when full judgment dominates), and therefore after Arvit these lights depart entirely — hence the need for the Shema on the bed, for the sake of the second midnight of the night. (Rabbi Yosef Chaim notes that all this is only the main points, as much as a simple person can bear in understanding, and that these matters contain further profound secrets explained at length in Sha'ar HaKavanot by our teacher the Ari.)
takeaways: The four recitations of the Shema (on the bed, Arvit, the sacrifices, Yotzer) are built in ascending levels, each one drawing light for a different higher union.

The Shema of the sacrifices was instituted because it is not possible to draw all the lights needed for Shacharit at once (in Yotzer alone) — so it is recited twice in sequence (sacrifices, then Yotzer), except for the ancient Vatikin of great holiness who managed with one.

The Shema of Minchah is unnecessary because the remaining light of Shacharit (a day of the quality of chesed) still remains; but the Shema of Arvit is not sufficient for midnight, so another Shema on the bed is required.

paragraphs: Qeriatah qodem hanetz hachamma dehaynu samuk lo bikde sheyyesayyem qeriat shema ubirkoteha im hanetz hachamma, veyismok hattepilla miyyad behanetz hachamma, umi sheyyukal laasot ken mitzva gedola beyado usekaro atzum gam bazzeman hazzeh sheen lanu koach kachasidim harishonim hanniqrain vatiqin, umikkol maqom im lo qeraah qodem hanetz hachamma yesh lo lehaqdim liqrotah bimhera kol mah sheyyukal, dizrizim maqdimin lemitzot: vehinneh zeman hanetz hachamma heela harab "bet david" za"l siman l"v dap y" shehu shaa achat qodem sheyyaaleh hashshemesh al haaretz veyeraeh lanu ayyen sham, ubitshubati besiyyata dishmayya besipre haq' "rab pealim" hebeti debarayv vekatabti deen reayot shello mukrachim deyesh lehashib, gam hebeti dibre "minchat kohen" v"ateret rosh" al berakot dap v denireh delet lehu sebarat ha"bet david" za"l mechosh hareot, deameru rabbotenu za"l bachatzot hayyom chamma berosh kol adam vaanachnu roin ki achar chamesh shaot vachetzi meet yetziat hachamma leenenu tihyeh chamma berosh kol adam, ak katabti dezeh hammibchan lo yaaleh ella bimot haqqayitz mah sheen ken bimot hachorep, veim ken en bazeh kede semika, vekatabti degiddule haacharonim lo matzinu shehebiu dibre harab "bet david" za"l lismok alehem veraq matzinu lehaggaon chida" b"machaziq beraka" siman n"ch shetztziyyen vehora maqom al seper "bet david" hannizkar gam behaggahotayv al zohar haqqadosh cheleq b dap qtz"v tziyyen al dibre "bet david" hannizkar velo gilla lanu haskamat dato leinyan halaka, umissipro "yosep ometz", siman "v ot g' shekkatab sham vezeh leshono" "amenam shamati ki meen dugma haya oseh maaseh harab haggadol ir veqaddish morenu harab rabbi yosep qubu leinyan tepillat hashshachar" ad kan leshono vediqdaqti mizzeh ki bizman haggaon chida" za"l lo hayu nohagin beir haqqodesh yerushalayim t"v veir haqqodesh chebron t"v laasot maaseh kisbarat harab "bet david" za"l, veal ken mah sheshshamanu omerim deatta minhag hachasidim bebet el ykb"tz beir haqqodesh yerushalayim t"v laasot kisbarat harab "bet david" biqriat shema utepilla hinneh zeh hu minhag chadash shello haya miqqodem, veharab hechasid hechasid mhr" minni nr"v katab derob hatztzibbur birushalayim tvb"b osim kemo shekkatab harab "bet david" za"l, amenam yesh medaqdeqim sheenam mitpallelim ki im achar yetziat hachamma mammash ukemo shekkatab beseper "dibre yosep" shevvartz dap "h veku', laken ani noheg legamero qeriat shema shishsha deqim shehu issur shaa qodem yetziat hashshemesh, velipamim mimmehirut hachazzan yihyeh yod o y"b deqim qodem yetziat hashshemesh al haaretz velo ikpat li, veken lipamim yihyeh im hashshemesh uleel shadday etchannan sheyyezakkennu labo al hannequdda shezzeh tzarik siata dishmayya ad kan leshono nr"v, vehinneh poh irenu y" pashat hamminhag miqqarob laasot biqriat shema utepilla kisbarat harab "bet david" za"l, ak vadday minhag hamdaqdeqim lehitpallel im yetziat hashshemesh mammash shenniret lanu, vehiqret shema yatchilu shishsha deqim qodem yetziat hashshemesh hu minhag nakon umeshubbach lepi qotzer dati:

clarification.explanation: The preferred time to recite the Shema is close to just before sunrise, so that one finishes the Shema and its blessings at sunrise and joins the [Amidah] prayer immediately at sunrise; whoever can do this has a great mitzvah and an immense reward, even in this era when we do not have the strength of the early pious ones (the Vatikin). Nevertheless, if one did not recite it before sunrise, he should hasten to recite it as soon as possible (for the diligent act early with mitzvot). Regarding the time of "sunrise," opinions differ: Rav Beit David wrote that it is one hour before the sun becomes visible to us over the land; the Ben Ish Chai (in Rav Pe'alim) disagreed that his proofs are not conclusive (and also that the test based on the sun's movement works only in summer, not winter), and that the great later authorities did not rely on him. It turns out that the custom of Beit El to pray according to Beit David is a new custom; and Rabbi Eliyahu Mani wrote that most of the congregation in Jerusalem follows Beit David, though there are meticulous people who pray only after the sun has actually risen — so he is accustomed to finish the Shema about six minutes before the sun's appearance. Recently the custom in our city has spread to follow Beit David; but in the Ben Ish Chai's own judgment, the custom of the meticulous — to pray with the sun's actual appearance, beginning the Shema about six minutes before — is the correct and praiseworthy one.
takeaways: Ideally one finishes reciting the Shema and its blessings at sunrise and joins the [Amidah] prayer immediately — a great mitzvah with an immense reward.

Opinions differ on the time of "sunrise": Beit David (one hour before the sun is visible) versus those who disagree; the Ben Ish Chai favors the custom of the meticulous — praying with the sun's actual appearance (beginning the Shema about six minutes before).

paragraphs: Im haya anus kol hallayla velo qara qeriat shema arbit ad sheala ammud hashshachar kevan sheadayin lo hanetz hachamma qore otah veyotze qetzat yede chobat qeriat shema dearbit, ap al pi dela mehanneya leh leinyan hattiqqunim hannaasim lemala, mihu lo yiqra oto hayyom qeriat shema shel shacharit ella ad achar hanetz hachamma deim ken havu lehu tarte desatere:

clarification.explanation: One who was under duress the entire night and did not recite the Shema of Arvit until dawn rose — since the sun has not yet risen, he recites it and thereby partially fulfills his obligation of the Shema of Arvit (though it will not benefit the rectifications accomplished above). But he should not recite the Shema of Shacharit that same day except after sunrise, so that there will not be two contradictory recitations at the same time.
takeaways: One under duress who did not recite Arvit — recites it until sunrise and partially fulfills the obligation.
The Shema of Shacharit that day is recited only after sunrise.

paragraphs: Zeman qeriat shema shel shacharit nimshak ad rebia hayyom beshaot zemanniyyot, vetzarik lehizzaher bimot hacherup shehayyom qatzar sheaz zeman qeriat shema hu qatzar, vead shaa achat achar rebia hayyom yakol liqrotah bebirkoteha abal en lo sakar keqore otah bizmannah, veim abar shaa achar rebia hayyom yiqraenna belo birkoteha keqore battora mishshum sapeq berakot lehaqel:

clarification.explanation: The time for the Shema of Shacharit extends until a quarter of the day (in seasonal hours), and one must be careful in the winter months when the day is short and its time is short. Until one hour after a quarter of the day he can still recite it with its blessings, but he does not have the reward of one who recites it in its proper time. And if an hour after a quarter of the day has passed, he should recite it without its blessings, like one reading in the Torah, on account of the doubt regarding blessings, to be lenient.
takeaways: The time for the Shema is until a quarter of the day; until an hour after that — with blessings but without the full reward.
After that hour — without blessings.

paragraphs: Qodem sheyyiqra qeriat shema yekavven leqayyem mitzvat aseh shennitztavvinu liqro qeriat shema shette peamim bayyom kemo shekkatub "vedibbarta bam veku' beshakebbeka ubequmeka" (debarim v, z), gam yekavven leqayyem mitzvat aseh leyached et hashshem, veyisgor enayv beyad yemino bepasuq rishon ad sheyyashlim "baruk shem kebod malkuto leolam vaed" veyesh sod baddabar, veim lo kivven libbo bappasuq "shema yisrael" bipshatan shel debarim lo yatza yede chobato vetzarik lachazor, veim hirgish beatzmo tekep achar sheamar pasuq "shema" lo yachzor lomar pasuq shema paam shenit deomer "shema shema" meshatteqin oto shello yihyeh nireh kemodeh lishte reshuyot chas veshalom, ella yishtoq shiur amirat parasha rishona veachar kak yachazor lomar pasuq "shema" veyiqra mishsham veelak al hasseder, veim yirtzeh shello yishtoq ella gomer kol happarasha harishona vechozer veqore shenit min pasuq "shema" in haki name yaaseh kak, vah adip mishshetiqa, vegam pasuq "baruk shem kebod malkuto leolam vaed" yesh omerim im ella ameru bekavvana chozer leomero bekavvana, mihu keshechozer baabur "baruk shem kebod malkuto leolam vaed" chozer min pasuq shema kede sheyyabo sod tiqqun pesuqim ellu al hasseder:

clarification.explanation: Before the Shema he should intend to fulfill the positive commandment to recite the Shema twice a day, and to unify the Name. He should close his eyes with his right hand during the first verse until he completes "Baruch Shem Kevod Malchuto Le'olam Va'ed." If he did not direct his heart to the plain meaning of the words in the verse "Shema Yisrael," he has not fulfilled his obligation and must repeat it, but he should not say "Shema, Shema" (which would appear as acknowledging two authorities); rather he should pause, and then go back from the verse "Shema," or finish the whole paragraph and then repeat — and this is preferable. Likewise, if he did not say "Baruch Shem" with proper intention, some hold that he goes back to say it with intention, starting from the verse "Shema."
takeaways: He intends to fulfill the commandment and to unify the Name, and closes his eyes during the first verse.
If he erred in intention, he goes back from "Shema" — but never says "Shema" twice in immediate succession.

paragraphs: Bappasuq "shema yisrael" yaaseh pisqe hattebot kol shette tebot beyachad, kede lekavven bahem kepi hammashmaut haachat, vehu ki shema perusho qabbala kemo "shemor veshameat" (debarim yb, kch) targumo "tar uteqabbel", vegam hu leshon habana "shema" kelomar "habben", veken hu kan omer "shema yisrael" kelomar qabbel debarim ellu vehebinam vetidam shettaamin bam vehu ki Adonai hu elohenu, veod hinneh hu Adonai echad, venimtza bazeh yesh qabbala vehodaa bishte debarim haechad hu qabbalat malkut shamayim beomero "Adonai elohenu" demodeh sheqqibbalnu elohuto lihyot lanu leelohha vaanachnu abadim lo, vehashsheni hu inyan yichud hashshem beomero "Adonai echad" shehu beli shittup acher sheen lo sheni kemo sheamar eliyyahu zakur lattob, ant hu chad vela bechosheban:

clarification.explanation: In the verse "Shema Yisrael" he should pause between each two words, to direct the intention. "Shema" means to accept and understand — accept these words and understand that Hashem is our God and that He is One. The verse contains two acknowledgments: the first is accepting the yoke of Heaven ("Hashem Eloheinu" — that we have accepted His divinity upon us), and the second is the unification of the Name ("Hashem Echad" — that He has no second and no other partnership with Him).
takeaways: Pause between the words of the first verse in order to direct the intention to its meaning.
The verse includes both accepting the yoke of Heaven (Hashem Eloheinu) and unifying the Name (Hashem Echad).

paragraphs: Ot ayi"n d"shema" veot d' d"echad" hem otiyyot gedolot, vekatab beseper "keter malkut" ketibat yad sheggam haqqore tzarik lekavven otam bemachshabto beotiyyot gedolot, ki haqqore tzarik letzayyer kol otiyyot happasuq leneged enayv bemachshabto ushette otiyyot ellu yetzayyerem beotiyyot gedolot vehu nakon:

clarification.explanation: The letter Ayin in the word "Shema" and the letter Dalet in the word "Echad" are written large. The reader should visualize in his mind all the letters of the verse before his eyes, and picture these two letters as large.
takeaways: One mentally pictures the letters of the verse, with the Ayin and the Dalet as large.

paragraphs: Betebat "echad" yekavven beshillub hvy"h dn"y shehu yhdvnh"y, vikavven sheyyihyu shavim beachdut echad vedabar zeh yekavven beshitchiyyut peshat millat "echad", ak yaarik bedale"t d"echad", vikavven beet shemmaarik bo limsor atzmo bisqila serepa harag cheneq al qiddush hashshem, vegam yekavven sheal yede qabbala zo yitkapperu peshaayv veyaalu nepesh rucha uneshama shello miyyayin nuqbin libchinat v"h shebbashshem, umishsham yaalu libchinat y"h, umishsham libchinat qotzo shel yo"d ad rum hammaalot, veim yesh lo yedia besod Adonai veyukal leharchib hakkavvana shello az yosip lekavven od sheyyimmashek shepa min en sop leattiqa qaddisha, umeattiqa qaddisha leabba veimma, umin abba veimma lezakar uneqeba:

clarification.explanation: In the word "Echad," one should intend the combination of the Name Havayah with the Name Adnut, pronounced "Yah-ha-do-na-hai," intending that the two Names unite as one — this is the plain intention embedded in the word "Echad" itself. He should lengthen the letter Dalet of "Echad," and while lengthening it, give up his life in his mind for the sanctification of the Name (as though ready for stoning, burning, execution, and strangulation). He should intend that through this acceptance his transgressions be atoned for, and that his soul — the nefesh, ruach, and neshamah within him — rise as mayin nukvin, first to the aspect of Vav-Heh of the Name, and from there to the aspect of Yud-Heh of the Name, and from there further up to the tip of the letter Yud, the very height of the levels. And whoever has knowledge of the secret of Hashem and can broaden his intention should further intend that thereby abundance is drawn from the Ein Sof to Atika Kadisha, and from Atika Kadisha to Abba and Imma, and from Abba and Imma to Zachar and Nekevah.
takeaways: He lengthens the Dalet of "Echad" and gives up his life for the sanctification of the Name, while intending the union of Havayah and Adnut (Yah-ha-do-na-hai) as one.

He intends atonement for transgressions and the ascent of the soul through the levels of Vav-Heh, Yud-Heh, and the tip of the Yud; and one with deeper knowledge adds the intention of drawing abundance from the Ein Sof down to Zachar and Nekevah.

paragraphs: Tebat "echad" nequdda besegol veqamatz, lekak yemaher biqriat haale"p dehassegol hu tenua qetanna velo yemaher biqriat hache"t deqamatz shehi tenua gedola, gam millebad zeh tzarik shello yaarik beale"p kede shello yitraeh keomer "i chad" rotzeh lomar "in chad, chas veshalom vekannizkar baacharonim, veap al pi deamarnu leel sheyyaarik bedale"t d"echad" tzarik lehizzaher shello yattiz haddelet bechozeq shennireh keomer "da", ella yaarik bah bemibta repuya velo degusha:

clarification.explanation: The word "Echad" is vocalized with a segol (under the Alef) and a kamatz (under the Chet). Therefore he should say the Alef quickly (a short vowel) and not say the Chet quickly (a long vowel), and he should also not lengthen the Alef, so that it will not sound like "ei chad" (as if there were no One, God forbid). And although he lengthens the Dalet, he must be careful not to snap it forcefully (so that it sounds like "da"), but rather lengthen it with a soft, not hard, pronunciation.
takeaways: He says the Alef of "Echad" quickly and lengthens the Dalet, with a soft pronunciation.
He is careful that it not sound like "ei chad" nor like "da."

paragraphs: Yapsiq qetzat ben pasuq "shema" lepasuq "baruk shem kebod malkuto leolam vaed", veken yapsiq qetzat ben pasuq "baruk shem kebod malkuto leolam vaed" lepasuq "veahabta", ukesheomer pasuq "baruk shem kebod malkuto leolam vaed" yarkin rosho qetzat lematta betebat malkuto, veyesh sod baddabar lehorid heara el hashshekina malkut aqeret habbayit, veap al gab deomerim "baruk shem kebod malkuto leolam vaed" belachash mikkol maqom yashmia leazenayv qetzat:

clarification.explanation: He should pause slightly between the verse "Shema" and "Baruch Shem Kevod Malchuto Le'olam Va'ed," and likewise between "Baruch Shem" and "Ve'ahavta." When he says "Baruch Shem Kevod Malchuto," he should bow his head slightly at the word "Malchuto," there being a secret in this, to draw down illumination to the Shechinah. And although he says "Baruch Shem" in a whisper, he should let it be heard somewhat to his own ears.
takeaways: He pauses slightly between the verses and bows his head at the word "Malchuto."
He says "Baruch Shem" in a whisper but still lets it be heard to his own ears.

paragraphs: Haqqore qeriat shema tzarik lehashmia leazenayv mah shemmotzi mippiv, ubediabad im lo hishmia leazenayv yatza, veotam hannohagim lomar pasuq "hishshameru" upasuq "vechara" belachash tzerikin lehizzaher sheyyashmiu leazenam lekattechilla:

clarification.explanation: One who recites the Shema must let what comes from his mouth be heard by his own ears; after the fact, if he did not let it be heard, he has fulfilled his obligation. Those accustomed to saying the verse "Hishamru" and the verse "Vechara" in a whisper must be careful to let them be heard by their ears from the outset.
takeaways: One should let the words of the Shema be heard by his own ears (after the fact, he has fulfilled the obligation even without this).
Even verses said in a whisper should be let heard by his ear.

paragraphs: Haqqore qeriat shema ben deshacharit ben dearbit ben qeriat shema deal hammitta hare zeh lo yirmoz beenayv, velo yiqrotz bispatayv, velo yeraeh beetzbeotayv beparasha rishona apillu letzorek mitzva, abal beparasha sheniyya veelak shari letzorek mitzva davqa, veshello letzorek mitzva asur, vehamrammez leqatan beenayv o beyadayv kede sheyyitpallel chashib letzorek mitzva apillu shezzeh qatan sheadayin lo nitchayyeb bitpilla, veotam gabbaim shettopesim beyadam quppa umechazzerim al haqqahal ligbot tzedaqa lo yaasu ken beet sheqqorin qeriat shema, vaapillu shehu tzorek mitzva dekevan dehu mehallek vegobeh beodo qore have lah qeria shel aray, veken poh irenu derek bene adam lehanip leatzmam bimnipa qetanna baqqayitz mippene hachom, tzarik lehazhiram shello yanipu beyadam bishat qeriat shema, ub"chesed laalapim" siman s"d ot Adonai katab tzarik lehizzaher mishsheibat apar htbq"v veqinnucha hachotem apillu bashsheniyya ubashshelishit vaapillu im yishtoq beet sheiba veqinnucha gam ken asur ayyen sham, venireh li beqinnucha hachotem lav kol appayya shavin delipamim harir yored meelayv veim lo yemaher leqanneach yored al sepatayv veyimmaes beatzmo vegam acherim yimmaasu immo, veameru rabbotenu za"l gadol kebod habberiyyot sheddocheh lo taaseh, ubiprat sheggorem sheyyitmaasu acherim veqasheh lahem meod biprat leistenis, laken nireh li kol kehay gavna yeqannach vaapillu beparasha rishona veraq yishtoq et sheyyeqannach:

clarification.explanation: One who recites the Shema should not gesture with his eyes, wink with his lips, or make signs with his fingers during the first paragraph, even for the sake of a mitzvah; from the second paragraph onward it is permitted for the sake of a mitzvah alone. Charity collectors should not collect during the Shema (since walking while collecting makes the recitation a casual one), and one fanning himself due to heat should be careful not to fan himself during the Shema. Likewise, one should not sniff tobacco. But regarding wiping the nose, when mucus runs down on its own and would make him and those around him repulsed, he should wipe it even during the first paragraph (remaining silent while wiping), for the sake of human dignity.
takeaways: One does not gesture with eyes or fingers during the first paragraph, and does not fan himself or collect charity [during the Shema].
Wiping a nose that has become repulsive is permitted even during the first paragraph, done in silence.

paragraphs: Haya mehallek badderek veratza liqrot qeriat shema tzarik laamod ad "lebabeka" veyesh omerim day bepasuq rishon v"baruk shem kebod malkuto leolam vaed" veharokeb al gabbe behema yaamid habbehema bepasuq rishon v"baruk shem kebod malkuto leolam vaed", abal hayyosheb beqaron en tzarik laamod:

clarification.explanation: One walking along the road who wishes to recite the Shema must stand still until "levavecha" (some say it suffices for the first verse and "Baruch Shem"). One riding an animal should halt it for the first verse and "Baruch Shem," but one sitting in a wagon need not stand still.
takeaways: One walking stands still for the first verse; one riding halts the animal; one sitting in a wagon is exempt.

paragraphs: Mi sherotzeh lehachmir al atzmo laamod keshehu yosheb kede liqrot qeriat shema meummad niqra abaryan im oseh ken bishbil chumera, abal im oseh ken kede lehaabir hashshena muttar vekannizkar baacharonim za"l:

clarification.explanation: One who is sitting and wishes to be stringent with himself by standing to recite the Shema while standing is called a transgressor if he does so for the sake of stringency. But if he stands in order to drive away sleep, it is permitted.
takeaways: One should not be stringent by standing for the Shema while sitting.
Standing in order to drive away sleep is permitted.

paragraphs: Ap al gab demishshurat haddin hu deim haya omed belav haki verotzeh liqro qeriat shema meummad mishshum denocha lo baamida behahi shata deeno mechuyyab lesheb kede leqareah meyushshab, mikkol maqom kepi hassod yosheb adip meummad, ukemo shekkatabti besipri haq' "mqbtzyl" middibre rabbenu haari"y za"l beshaar hakkavvanot derush v detzarik atta leorer sod hayyichud lemala behetenu lematta beolam habberia velaken adip lesheb, mippene shehayyeshiba moreh sheanachnu odennu beolam habberia deen amida ella baatzilut vekannizkar sham:

clarification.explanation: Although according to strict law, one who is already standing and finds it comfortable may recite the Shema standing, nevertheless according to the secret [teaching], sitting is preferable to standing. The reason is that one must arouse the secret of the union above while we are below in the World of Beriah, and sitting indicates that we are still in the World of Beriah (for true standing belongs only to the World of Atzilut), as mentioned there.
takeaways: According to the secret [teaching], it is preferable to recite the Shema seated.

paragraphs: Sapeq qara qeriat shema sapeq lo qara tzarik liqrot, diqriat shema hi min hattora usepeq tora lechumera, vaapillu lemaen deamar pasuq echad o parasha achat dedavqa hem min hattora, chayyab liqrot missapeq kol shelosh parashiyyot, shekkak hayeta hattaqqana kol zeman sheyyiqra qeriat shema shel tora sheyyiqra hashshelosh parashiyyot lepikak hammitnamnem beemtza im yodea beberur shessiyyem parasha rishona chozer mipparasha sheniyya, veim eno yodea hekan hu chozer larosh, veim hipsiq beemtza qeriat shema mechamat ones kegon sheasa hattinoq tzerakayv vehukrach lishtoq, im shaha kede ligmor et kullah dehaynu merosh qeriat shema vead sopah tzarik lachazor lerosh, abal im hipsiq shello mechamat ones ki im birtzono, sheim haya rotzeh haya yakol liqrot, az apillu im shaha zeman rab vaapillu im hipsiq bedibbur en tzarik lachazor ella lammaqom sheppasaq:

clarification.explanation: One who is in doubt whether he recited the Shema must recite it, since the Shema is from the Torah and a doubt in a matter of the Torah is resolved stringently, and he recites all three paragraphs. One who dozes off in the middle: if he knows for certain he finished the first paragraph, he goes back from the second; if he does not know where he stopped, he goes back to the beginning. If he was interrupted due to an unavoidable circumstance (such as needing to be silent) and the pause lasted long enough to have finished the whole reading, he must go back to the beginning; but if he stopped voluntarily (that is, he could have continued had he wished), even if he paused a long time or spoke, he need only go back to where he stopped.
takeaways: In doubt whether he recited it — he recites all three paragraphs; in doubt where he stopped — he goes back to the beginning.
An interruption due to an unavoidable circumstance, lasting as long as the whole reading, requires going back to the beginning; a voluntary interruption requires returning only to where he stopped.

paragraphs: Qara qeriat shema veniknas lebet hakkeneset umatza tzibbur sheqqorin qeriat shema chayyab liqrot immahem pasuq rishon v"baruk shem kebod malkuto leolam vaed", umikkol maqom tob sheyyiqra immahem kol haqriat shema ad hassop viqabbel sakar keqore battora, veim hatztzibbur qorin qeriat shema vehu omed bizmirot achar sheamar baruk sheamar, az yishtoq beod sheqqorin pasuq shema v"baruk shem kebod malkuto leolam vaed" veyisgor enayv viharher pasuq shema v"baruk shem kebod malkuto leolam vaed", abal im omed beqarebbanot o betachanunim sherashshay lehapsiq, hare zeh poseq veqore immahem pasuq rishon v"baruk shem kebod malkuto leolam vaed":

clarification.explanation: One who already recited the Shema and entered the synagogue to find the congregation reciting the Shema must recite the first verse and "Baruch Shem" together with them (and it is good to recite the whole thing with them and receive the reward of one reading Torah). If he is standing in the Pesukei DeZimra (after "Baruch SheAmar") — he should be silent while they recite the verse and close his eyes and think it through in his mind; but if he is standing in Korbanot or in the supplications, where interruption is permitted, he interrupts and recites the first verse and "Baruch Shem" aloud with them.
takeaways: He recites the first verse with the congregation even though he already recited the Shema.
During Pesukei DeZimra he is silent and thinks it through; during Korbanot or supplications he interrupts and recites it aloud.

paragraphs: Im lo hinnicha tepillin venizdammenu lo achar shehitchil "yotzer", mannichan ben happeraqim umebarek alehem, veellu hen ben happeraqim ben beraka rishona libraka sheniyya, uben sheniyya l"shema", uben "shema" l"vehaya im shema", ben v"haya im shamoa" l"veyomar", abal ben "veyomar" l"emet veyatztzib" lo yapsiq dekan nechshab emtza happereq, vekol zeh hu bitpillin mippene dechoba liqro qeriat shema bitpillin lekak yebarek alayv, abal im lo hinnicha tzitzit venizdammen lo tzitzit yannichennu ben happeraqim belo beraka, veachar tepillat shemoneh esreh yemashmesh bo vibarek:

clarification.explanation: One who did not don tefillin, and they became available to him after he had already begun "Yotzer," puts them on between the sections and recites the blessing over them. The divisions between sections are: between the blessings, and between the second blessing and "Shema," and between the paragraphs; but between "Vayomer" and "Emet VeYatziv" he should not interrupt (as this is considered the middle of a section). This applies to tefillin, since there is an obligation to recite the Shema while wearing them, and therefore he recites the blessing. But tzitzit that became available to him — he puts them on between the sections without a blessing, and handles them and recites the blessing after the Amidah.
takeaways: Tefillin that become available — he puts them on between the sections and recites the blessing.
Tzitzit that become available — he puts them on without a blessing, and recites the blessing after the prayer.

paragraphs: Laaniyyat qaddish uqedushsha v"baraku" v"modim" vachamishsha ummanim rishonim deqaddish poseq apillu beemtza happereq, vaapillu beemtza happasuq. ak keshepposeq beemtza happasuq veoneh. chozer achar kak letachat oto pasuq bekol open sheyyihyeh mihu beemtza pasuq "shema yisrael" veken beemtza pasuq "baruk shem kebod malkuto leolam vaed", veken ben pasuq "shema" leben pasuq "baruk shem kebod malkuto leolam vaed" al yapsiq kelal lekol dabar shebbiqdushsha. veim qareu oto leseper tora vehu omed beemtza qeriat shema lo yaaleh apillu qareu oto bishmo, mihu im yukal ligmor et haqriat shema kullah ad sheyyaggia labbima veyomar gam ken "emet veyatztzib veku'", ad "haddabar hazzeh alenu leolam vaed" veachar kak yebarek al hattora veyiqra, yaaseh ken:

clarification.explanation: To respond to Kaddish, Kedushah, "Barechu," "Modim," and the first five "Amens" of Kaddish, he interrupts even in the middle of a section and even in the middle of a verse, and when interrupting in the middle of a verse, he goes back afterward to the beginning of that verse. But in the middle of the verse "Shema Yisrael" and "Baruch Shem," and between the two verses, he should not interrupt at all for anything of sanctity. If he was called to the Torah while in the middle of the Shema, he should not go up, even if called by name — unless he can finish the entire Shema, including "Emet VeYatziv" until "this matter is upon us forever," by the time he reaches the platform, in which case he should do so and then recite the blessing over the Torah and read.
takeaways: He interrupts for matters of sanctity even in the middle of a section, but not during the first verse itself.
If called to the Torah in the middle of the Shema, he does not go up unless he can finish it by the time he reaches the platform.

paragraphs: Kesheyyaggia l"uqeshartam leot al yadeka" yemashmesh bitpillin shel yad, "vehayu letotapot" yemashmesh bitpillin shel rosh, veken yaaseh bappasuq "uqeshartam otam" vekannizkar beseper hakkavvanot, veap al gab dekatabnu leel beshabbat haqqodem deyotzer hu baolam habberia velo yenashsheq ella raq bitpillin shel yad, haka shane shehu memashmesh umenashsheq bishbil chibbub mitzva, lekak yemashmesh bishnehem kaasher nizkarim shettehem bakkatub:

clarification.explanation: When he reaches "and you shall bind them as a sign upon your hand" he handles the tefillin of the hand, and at "and they shall be as frontlets" the tefillin of the head, and likewise at "and you shall bind them." Although in the blessings of the Shema (Yotzer) one kisses only the tefillin of the hand, here it is different — he handles and kisses both, out of love and cherishing of the mitzvah, since both are mentioned in the verse.
takeaways: He handles the tefillin of the hand and of the head when they are mentioned in the Shema.
He handles and kisses both, out of love for the mitzvah.

paragraphs: Kesheyyomar "ureitem oto" yistakkel batztzitziyyot shebbeyado shene peamim bezo achar zo, veachar kol paam mishte happeamim ellu yaabirem al gabbe enayv, ubeet shemmistakkel bahem yekavven mispar ayin hu chamishsha hvyv"t vinashsheqem achar kak, veken beomero "veachare enekem" yaabirem al gabbe enayv vinashsheqem, veyesh sod baddabar hazzeh:

clarification.explanation: When he says "and you shall see it," he looks at the tzitzit in his hand twice, one after the other, and after each time passes them over his eyes. While looking at them he intends that the numerical value of "ayin" (eye) corresponds to the five appearances of the Name Havayah, and afterward kisses them. Likewise when he says "and after your eyes," he passes them over his eyes and kisses them, there being a secret in this.
takeaways: He looks at the tzitzit twice at "and you shall see it," passing them over his eyes and kissing them.
He does the same at "and after your eyes."
